headline: TensorWave Signs 457MW, Six-Year Compute Deal With OpenAI on AMD MI455X Helios Racks
raw_snippet: TensorWave signed a six-year deal to provide OpenAI with 457MW of dedicated compute on AMD MI455X Helios racks in US data centers. Capacity starts coming online in H1 2027, with full deployment by early 2028. The deal adds to OpenAI's 6GW AMD commitment, delivered through a neocloud rather than directly.

headline: Nvidia Scaled Back Commitment to OpenAI's Piketon, Ohio Data-Center Lease
raw_snippet: WSJ reports that in August Nvidia cut back how much it committed to OpenAI's data-center lease in Piketon, Ohio. OpenAI signed the lease with SoftBank's SB Energy, and Nvidia pulled back after CFO (now interim CEO) Colette Kress became skeptical. UBS estimates $50B+ in neocloud financing could leave the market.

headline: Effingham County, GA Approves OpenAI's $20B Project Camellia Data Center Site Plan
raw_snippet: Effingham County, GA commissioners voted Tuesday evening (Nov 17) to approve the site plan for OpenAI's Project Camellia data center: six buildings on 1,300+ acres. The vote had been postponed Nov 3 over berm and wetland questions. A proposed moratorium on future data center applications would not apply to Camellia.

headline: All 14GW of OpenAI's Planned US Data-Center Capacity in States Whose Governors Back Construction Pause
raw_snippet: WSJ reports that all ~14GW of OpenAI's planned US data-center capacity is in states whose governors back a construction pause. About 10GW is at SB Energy's PORTS-Pike campus in Ohio; the rest in Georgia and Texas. Rivals are less exposed: 45% of Microsoft's and 42% of Amazon's planned capacity is in pause-backing states.

headline: Cerebras Running Behind Schedule on OpenAI Data-Center Capacity Tranches; Shares Down ~6%
raw_snippet: Cerebras said on its Nov 12 Q3 call that it is 'running behind schedule on initial tranches' of data-center capacity owed to OpenAI under the 750MW take-or-pay inference deal (~$20B+). CEO Feldman blamed delays 'exclusively' on land, power and shell. CBRS fell ~6% intraday on Nov 16.

headline: Samsung SDS in Early Talks to Host OpenAI and Anthropic in Korean AI Data Centers
raw_snippet: FT reports that Samsung SDS (Samsung's IT services arm) is in early talks to sign OpenAI and Anthropic as tenants in its Korean AI data centers. No contract, capacity, site, price or timing disclosed. Builds on Oct 2025 OpenAI-Samsung Stargate Korea agreements.

headline: Nvidia Narrows When Its $105B Ohio Data-Center Guarantee for OpenAI Kicks In
raw_snippet: Nvidia's new CFO commentary says its loan guarantees, including the $105B backstop for OpenAI's PORTS-Pike campus in Ohio, only start once the customer has raised financing and installed Nvidia's compute. If the project stalls before that, the guarantee 'doesn't exist.' Kress had earlier cut the backstop from $250B to $105B.

headline: Nvidia Q3 Filing Details $105B Guarantee on OpenAI's Ohio Campus: 4.25GW, Nine Buildings, 20-Year Leases
raw_snippet: Nvidia Q3 CFO commentary details its guarantee for OpenAI's Ohio campus (SB Energy's PORTS-Pike site): covers about 4.25GW across nine buildings on 20-year leases, with max exposure of $105B. First building expected in Nvidia's fiscal 2029. Nvidia also has an option to back about 3.8GW more. Total lease guarantees now $118B.

headline: OpenAI Explored $5 Billion-Plus Acquisition of AI Interpretability Startup Goodfire
raw_snippet: OpenAI held talks in recent months with AI startup Goodfire over a possible acquisition or partnership valued at $5B+. CEO Sam Altman was particularly interested in the work of Nick Cammarata, a former OpenAI researcher now at Goodfire, whose essay on neural network interpretability has caused debate among AI researchers.

headline: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Digital Wallet for Dot Assistant Online Purchases
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced a ChatGPT digital wallet on Friday, giving the company's 'Dot' assistant a new way to buy things online without directly accessing shoppers' card details. The wallet enables commerce transactions through the AI assistant.

headline: OpenAI Disbands Standalone Robotics Team, Believes General Models Can Control Robots Directly
raw_snippet: OpenAI is disbanding its standalone robotics team, believing that general models like GPT-6 Astra can control robots directly, Fortune reported. The move signals OpenAI's strategic shift away from dedicated robotics research toward integrating robot control into its frontier models.

headline: Sam Altman at DealBook Summit: OpenAI IPO Will Come 'At Some Point,' Stresses AI Safety
raw_snippet: At the NYT DealBook Summit, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said the company's IPO would come 'at some point,' downplaying valuation fluctuations and saying the 'trend is going to be strong.' OpenAI President Greg Brockman stressed AI safety as a cultural shift. Altman and Brockman discussed balancing safety with AI development progress.

headline: Sam Altman Warns of Chip-Demand Double Counting by New Vendors, Confirms Eventual OpenAI IPO
raw_snippet: On Semafor's Future Proof podcast, Sam Altman warned that many new chip vendors are each telling the supply chain that AI labs will buy most of their output — the same demand counted repeatedly. He confirmed OpenAI will eventually IPO, citing 'real downsides' to being public but arguing the world deserves exposure to AI's value creation.
